title: Lexer Token Streams
description: Breaks raw source text into a stream of tokens - keywords, identifiers, literals, operators - which is the first step of any transpiler. A correct lexer handles edge cases like nested comments and string escapes, because every later stage trusts its output completely.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Recursive-Descent Parsers
description: Builds the syntax tree with a set of mutually recursive functions, one per grammar rule, which makes the parser easy to read and debug. Hand-written recursive descent gives precise error messages at the cost of manual grammar maintenance.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: AST Normalization
description: Rewrites the parsed tree into a canonical shape - flattening nested expressions, desugaring shortcuts - so later passes deal with fewer cases. Normalization shrinks the transform logic dramatically because every construct has exactly one representation.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Desugaring Passes
description: Expands syntactic sugar - async/await, spread, optional chaining - into simpler core constructs the backend already understands. Desugaring early lets the transpiler support new syntax by adding small passes instead of rewriting the code generator.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Polyfill Injection
description: Detects modern APIs used in the source and injects small compatibility shims so the output runs on older runtimes. Injection is usage-driven - only the APIs actually referenced get polyfilled - keeping output lean.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Syntax Lowering
description: Translates high-level constructs like classes and modules into lower-level equivalents the target runtime supports natively. Lowering is where class syntax becomes prototype chains and modules become wrapper functions, done mechanically and repeatably.

fields.pitfall: lowered code is harder to debug

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Source-Map Emission
description: Emits source maps alongside transpiled output so debuggers and error trackers map generated positions back to original source lines. Without maps, production stack traces point at unreadable generated code and debugging becomes guesswork.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Tree-Shaking
description: Eliminates exported functions and modules that nothing imports, using static analysis of the module graph. Tree-shaking is why modern bundles stay small despite huge libraries: unused code never ships.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Minification
description: Compresses output by shortening names, removing whitespace and comments, and folding constant expressions. Minified code runs identically but downloads faster, which directly improves load time on slow networks.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-Language Transpilation
description: Converts entire programs from one language to another - Python to JavaScript, Java to Kotlin - by mapping idioms, not just syntax. Faithful transpilation preserves semantics across different standard libraries and runtime models, which is far harder than same-language transforms.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Incremental Transpilation
description: Re-transpiles only the files that changed and their dependents, caching everything else. Incremental builds turn multi-minute transpiles into seconds, which is what makes large codebases pleasant to develop against.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Error Recovery Parsing
description: Continues parsing after syntax errors by skipping to synchronization points, collecting all errors in one pass instead of stopping at the first. Developers fix everything at once rather than playing whack-a-mole with one error per compile.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Macro Expansion
description: Expands compile-time macros into their generated code before the main transform passes run. Hygienic macros avoid variable capture bugs, making them safer than textual preprocessing while still enabling powerful code generation.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Type-Directed Transforms
description: Uses type information to guide transformations - choosing the right overload, inserting correct conversions, eliminating dead branches. Type-directed passes are more precise than purely syntactic ones because they understand what the code means, not just how it looks.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Idempotent Output
description: Guarantees that transpiling the output again produces the same output - the transform is a fixed point. Idempotence makes builds stable and lets tools safely re-run the transpiler without accumulating formatting or structural drift.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
